claims.statement: All existing books and related data survive the account transition.
An environment variable supplies the legacy account email.
Separate users register and sign in with email and password.
A public landing page explains the site.
The first release may continue saving to disk.
No Resend, verification, or password-reset flows.
The initial planning-only limit ended with explicit implementation authorization. Live rollout still requires separate approval.
Book and image access must check the server-resolved owner on every path.
Set a legacy password through a hidden offline prompt; never use public email matching to claim data.
Add ownerUserId and revision in existing book files while preserving disk paths and IDs.
Preserve inherited project and spatial data behind a legacy-account guard.
Use one server process and one account-aware storage version.
Reading an empty comic store creates three seed books.
Migration must bypass normalizers that rebuild objects and transform older fields.
Use isolated copies and synthetic fixtures for mutation and browser checks.

conflicts.resolution: The initial planning-only scope controlled planning. A later user request authorized implementation, commits, stacked PRs, and disposable checks.

shape.appetite: Small first release for one personal-project server. Reuse the comic editor and disk volume.
shape.problem: The shared library has no user identity or ownership boundary.

recommended_shape.storage: One user registry, per-session files, existing book/image paths.
recommended_shape.ownership: Stable UUID user IDs; ownerUserId and revision in books; images inherit book ownership.
recommended_shape.migration: Explicit stopped-writer migration with full verified backup, journal, raw additive transforms, and completion marker.
recommended_shape.auth: Node scrypt, opaque random session tokens, disk session lookup, same-origin writes.

success_moves: Prove content preservation on a disposable copy before account UI.
Keep IDs and storage paths stable.
Require server-resolved identity inside every comic store operation.
Guard inherited APIs and actions without expanding their product scope.
Retain drafts and reject saves after account change or revision conflict.
